description: We’re a team of 5 students taking on the Abandoned but not Forgotten challenge. Our goal is to turn dense NASA archives into an engaging, story-driven experience for younger and casual space fans bringing the retired rovers, landers, and instruments left on the Moon and Mars back to life and showing how their engineering shaped modern space science.
summary: Cosmic Relics is an interactive web application designed to inspire school-age space enthusiasts by telling the epic stories of NASA’s hardware left across the solar system. From the Apollo lunar modules on the Moon and silent rovers on Mars to the Voyager probes speeding through deep interstellar space, Cosmic Relics transforms historical telemetry into engaging, age-appropriate narratives. By combining interactive 3D solar system maps, bite-sized storybook chapters, and audio-guided logs, the platform introduces students to the engineering marvels and groundbreaking science behind humanity's greatest robotic and crewed emissaries. It addresses the challenge of making deep-space history accessible and exciting for young learners, sparking the next generation of scientists and explorers.
details:
What it does & how it works: Cosmic Relics features an interactive 3D solar system dashboard. Users navigate across three zones—The Moon, Mars, and Deep Space—to discover historical hardware (e.g., Apollo descent stages, Curiosity/Perseverance rovers, Voyager 1 & 2). Clicking an object opens an interactive "Mission Log" containing its launch history, operational status, and simplified science breakdowns. It also features a "Code a Signal" mini-game.

Benefits & Intended Impact: Fosters STEM curiosity in K-12 students by turning aerospace history into a narrative adventure. It serves as an open-source educational resource for science classrooms.

Tools, Languages & Software:

  • Languages: JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3
  • Frameworks & Libraries: React.js, Three.js (for 3D hardware rendering), Tailwind CSS
  • Hosting & Tools: Vercel, Figma

Creativity & Design Considerations: We designed the interface like an interactive space journal rather than a dry technical report. High-contrast colors, playful iconography, and audio narration options ensure accessibility for younger children.
